## ADM Final Assignment

by Can Idil and Femke Dhondt.

R markdown for visualising the testing & simulation results.

# Preparing for data

First we have to import the packages we have use for.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

```

After that, we define a function which will allow us, for the .CSVs our main.py outputs, to plot any given metric against the varying threshold value, across different loads.

```{r}
plot_metric_vs_threshold <- function(metric, loads_to_show = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5)) {
  sub <- threshold_algosr2 %>% filter(L %in% loads_to_show)
  base_sub <- baselinesr2 %>% filter(L %in% loads_to_show)
 
  ggplot(sub, aes(threshold, .data[[metric]], color = family)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(data = base_sub, aes(yintercept = .data[[metric]], linetype = algorithm),
               color = "grey40") +
    facet_wrap(~ L, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_both) +
    labs(title = paste(metric, "vs. threshold, across load levels"),
         linetype = "Baseline", color = "Algorithm family") +
    theme_minimal()
}

```

# Prepare the data

We then import our .CSV file and create a family variable that will allow us to group the respective algorithms (for ease of use).

```{r}
r2 <- read_csv("results_lowq_rand_basic_1000.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    family = case_when(
      str_detect(algorithm, "^Online Threshold")   ~ "Online Threshold",
      TRUE ~ algorithm   # the two baselines keep their own name
    ),
    threshold = as.numeric(str_extract(algorithm, "[0-9.]+$"))
  )

baselinesr2 <- r2 %>% filter(is.na(threshold))
threshold_algosr2 <- r2 %>% filter(!is.na(threshold))

```

# Visualise the data

We can now visualise the main metrics we have available to us.

```{r}
plot_metric_vs_threshold("avg_rank")

plot_metric_vs_threshold("avg_distance")

plot_metric_vs_threshold("matched_rate")
ggsave("plot_match_random_n1000_q1q25.png", width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150)

plot_metric_vs_threshold("blocking_pairs")
ggsave("plot_block_random_n1000_q1q25.png", width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150)

```

We then observe what the minimum number of blocking pairs is per algorithm, per load; and look at the corresponding distance threshold values for our algorithm.
We also plot those threshold values against the load values.

```{r}
optimal_per_load <- threshold_algosr2 %>%
  group_by(L) %>%
  slice_min(blocking_pairs, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(L, threshold, blocking_pairs, matched_rate)

optimal_per_load

ggplot(optimal_per_load, aes(L, threshold)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Blocking minimising threshold, per load",
       y = expression(tau^"*"))
ggsave("plot_block_min_per_load.png", width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150)

```

We then make a plot to compare the number of blocking pairs for our algorithm, per load, per threshold. We also include a black dot to show where the respective local minima are for each threshold. 

```{r}
ggplot(threshold_algosr2, aes(threshold, blocking_pairs, color = factor(L), group = L, linewidth = L)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = optimal_per_load, aes(threshold, blocking_pairs),
             color = "black", size = 4, shape = 18) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "C") +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.3: 1.5)) +     # thin for low L, thick for high L
  guides(linewidth = "none", col=guide_legend(reverse=TRUE)) +               
  labs(title = "Blocking pairs vs. threshold, all loads overlaid",
       subtitle = "black dots mark each load's minimum; thicker line = higher load",
       color = "L")

ggsave("plot_block_min_per_load_comparison.png", width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150)

```

# Extra testing

Some extra testing to make sure $q_max$ doesn't matter, and to make visuals for the presentation.

First for $q_max = 16$. Just repeat the same process as above.

```{r}

ggplot(threshold_algosr3, aes(threshold, blocking_pairs, color = factor(L), group = L, linewidth = L)) +

       color = "L")

ggsave("plot_block_min_per_load_comparison_q16.png", width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150)


```

# Extra with Shrinking Threshold

Include shrinking threshold to show poor performance with random preferences.

```{r}
r5 <- read_csv("results_q1q25_rand_basic+shrink_1000.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    family = case_when(
      str_detect(algorithm, "^Online Threshold")   ~ "Online Threshold",
      str_detect(algorithm, "^Shrinking Threshold") ~ "Shrinking Threshold",
      TRUE ~ algorithm   # the two baselines keep their own name
    ),
    threshold = as.numeric(str_extract(algorithm, "[0-9.]+$"))
  )

plot_metric_vs_threshold <- function(data, baseline_data, metric,
                                      loads_to_show = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0,
                                                         1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5)) {
  sub <- data %>% filter(L %in% loads_to_show)
  base_sub <- baseline_data %>% filter(L %in% loads_to_show)

  ggplot(sub, aes(threshold, .data[[metric]], color = family)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(data = base_sub, aes(yintercept = .data[[metric]], linetype = algorithm),
               color = "grey40") +
    facet_wrap(~ L, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_both) +
    labs(title = paste(metric, "vs. threshold, across load levels"),
         linetype = "Baseline", color = "Algorithm family") +
    theme_minimal()
}

baselinesr5 <- r5 %>% filter(is.na(threshold))
threshold_algosr5 <- r5 %>% filter(!is.na(threshold))

plot_metric_vs_threshold(threshold_algosr5, baselinesr5, "blocking_pairs")
ggsave("plot_compare_blocking_basic+shrink.png", width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150)

plot_metric_vs_threshold(threshold_algosr5, baselinesr5, "matched_rate")
ggsave("plot_compare_matched_basic+shirnk.png", width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150)


optimal_per_load <- threshold_algosr5 %>%
  group_by(L) %>%
  slice_min(blocking_pairs, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(L, threshold, blocking_pairs, matched_rate)

optimal_per_load

ggplot(threshold_algosr5, aes(threshold, blocking_pairs, color = factor(L), group = L, linewidth = L)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = optimal_per_load, aes(threshold, blocking_pairs),
             color = "black", size = 4, shape = 18) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "C") +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.3: 1.5)) +     # thin for low L, thick for high L
  guides(linewidth = "none", col=guide_legend(reverse=TRUE)) +               
  labs(title = "Blocking pairs vs. threshold, all loads overlaid, q_max=40",
       subtitle = "black dots mark each load's minimum; thicker line = higher load",
       color = "L")

```
